app.title: Auspice: interactive viewer for phylogenomic datasets
app.summary: A person opens a dataset (a tree of sampled genomes with metadata) from a dataset selector, and can drop extra metadata files onto the page. They colour the tree by a trait or a genotype, change its layout, and narrow it with typed filters, a date range slider and clade zooming. Clicking a tip or branch opens its details and mutations, while the map, genome diversity chart and frequency chart redraw for whatever is selected. They leave with the visible subset exported as tree files, metadata tables, figures or a dataset file, or with a narrative that walks readers through saved views.

task.text: Explore a tree of sampled genomes alongside where and when the samples came from and how their sequences vary, to identify and compare clades and share what is seen.

data.text: A tree of sampled sequences in which each tip and internal node carries dates, traits, locations and mutations, together with a genome annotation and optional frequency, measurement and root-sequence sidecar files.
data.item: a sampled genome: a tip on the tree with its date, traits, location and mutations

stage.text: exploring an inferred pathogen tree after the analysis pipeline, and presenting it to others

mechanism.text: A sidebar of colour, filter, date and layout controls drives linked panels: tree, map, diversity bar chart and frequency stream all share one colouring and one visible subset, and clicks in one panel (a deme, an entropy bar, a mutation) recolour or filter the others. A click on a tip or branch opens a detail panel, and every view state is kept in the URL so it can be shared or played as narrative slides.

field.text: phylogenetic and phylogeographic analysis of pathogen genomes in genomic epidemiology

workflow.name: explore a tree of samples through linked views and export the selected subset

steps.here: a dataset selector loads a dataset file from the server; CSV, TSV, Excel or node-data JSON files dropped on the page add new colourings, locations and filters

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: the tree is drawn in rectangular, radial, unrooted, clock (root-to-tip with regression) or scatter layout, coloured by any trait or by genotype at chosen positions, with a legend

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: typed filters by trait value, strain name or mutation; a date range slider with date pickers; clicking a branch zooms to its clade and 'focus on selected' shrinks the rest
click a tip or shift-click a branch for a panel with its traits, dates, accession and mutations grouped by gene; clicking a mutation recolours or filters the tree by it

the map shows demes sized by visible tip count and transmissions between them, animated over time; the entropy chart shows diversity per genome position, and a click colours the tree by that site; the frequency stream shows each colour group's share over time; a second tree can be drawn opposite as a tanglegram

a download modal saves the visible subset as Newick or annotated Nexus trees, metadata and acknowledgement TSVs, diversity TSV, a combined SVG of all panels, or the dataset JSON with the current view settings

distinctive: the tree can be laid out against sample date, with a root-to-tip regression giving a clock rate
per-position Shannon entropy or mutation counts across the genome annotation, with coding regions drawn as a navigable track
geographic spread is animated through time on the map, with inferred transmissions drawn between locations
two trees built from the same samples can be compared as a tanglegram with lines joining shared tips
markdown narratives step readers through saved view states slide by slide
